attachments.origin_landmark: lateral tibial condyle, proximal fibula, interosseous membrane

functional_compartments.name: Single fiber population
functional_compartments.function_note: Its 4 tendons pass under the extensor retinaculum and fan out to the extensor expansions of digits 2-5, mirroring extensor digitorum's arrangement in the hand.
functional_compartments.source: Ward SR, Eng CM, Smallwood LH, Lieber RL (2009) Clin Orthop Relat Res 467:1074-1082 -- lower-extremity muscle architecture (fascicle length, PCSA, sarcomere length) cadaver dataset

source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998); Ward SR, Eng CM, Smallwood LH, Lieber RL (2009) Clin Orthop Relat Res 467:1074-1082 -- lower-extremity muscle architecture (fascicle length, PCSA, sarcomere length) cadaver dataset

trigger_points.location_description: Muscle belly on the anterolateral shin, lateral to tibialis anterior, in the upper-to-middle third of the leg.
trigger_points.referred_pain_pattern: Pain distributed over the dorsum of the foot and along the anterior shin, with the distal referral concentrated over the middle toes (second through fourth) rather than the great toe.
trigger_points.activation_perpetuating_factors: Repetitive dorsiflexion (walking/running on uneven or soft ground), direct trauma to the shin, and immobilization; frequently activated together with tibialis anterior and extensor hallucis longus given their shared dorsiflexor function.
trigger_points.notes: Referral overlaps with tibialis anterior and extensor hallucis longus, so the three anterior-compartment muscles are usually examined together; can mimic anterior compartment syndrome or deep peroneal nerve irritation.
trigger_points.source: Simons, Travell & Simons Trigger Point Manual, Vol. 2 (Lower Extremities), 1999 -- as cited in secondary summaries (e.g. triggerpoints.net 'Extensor Digitorum Longus', Morningside Acupuncture NYC extensor digitorum longus trigger-point reference) describing the anterolateral-shin trigger point site and dorsal-foot/middle-toe referral pattern
